messages:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up — I'm proposing a ‘cut-and-mend’ playbook to surgically extract the enrichment logic out of `enrichment-service` into two narrower services (enricher-read, enricher-write). Goal: reduce hotpath surface area and make ownership clearer without a big-bang migration. High level steps in the playbook below.

jordan: Can you paste the TL;DR steps? I skimmed the RFC but want the exact cadence.

maya: TL;DR: 1) Add compatibility API on existing service, 2) Dual-write for a bounded window with feature flag + schema adapter, 3) Background KV copy job to seed the new read service, 4) Canary traffic (1%, 5%, 20%), 5) Promote and flip reads, 6) Decommission old endpoints after safety period.

sahil: Ops/observability note: we need tracing + span tags for both sides during dual-write. Also add a synthetic workload that exercises the long-tail seq lengths so we catch cache pressure regressions.

becka: SLA checkpoint — Dedicated customers in EU-1 have a 99.9% latency SLO. We must gate promotion on error-rate and tail-latency thresholds. If error_rate > 0.5% rollback immediately.

jordan: Data migration question: how do we handle concurrent writes between the two stores? eventual consistency ok for enrichment?

maya: Good call. Enrichment is best-effort and idempotent for our usecases. Plan: dual-write is write-through with best-effort retry; read-after-write consistency will be served from the old service until we flip reads. Background copier will prioritize recent keys first; we’ll use a monotonic seq token to resume.

oliver: For canary gating, propose these metrics (from least to most critical):
- p95 latency (user-facing)
- error rate (4xx/5xx aggregated)
- KV miss rate / cache hit ratio
- CPU/GPU utilization on serving pool
- request surge/backpressure events

oliver: Sample rollout config (prelim):
```yaml
rollout:
  phases:
    - name: canary-1
      pct: 1
      duration: 30m
      gates:
        error_rate: "<0.5%"
        p95_latency: "<350ms"
    - name: canary-2
      pct: 5
      duration: 1h
      gates:
        error_rate: "<0.3%"
        p95_latency: "<300ms"
    - name: gradual
      pct: 100
      duration: 24h
      gates:
        error_rate: "<0.2%"
        p95_latency: "<300ms"
```

sahil: Add a gate for tail-kv-miss: if miss spikes >10% we should pause — that usually indicates the copier lagging. Also emit a special span `migration.phase` in traces so we can query per-phase in Honeycomb.

maya: I'll open the migration job PR today and attach the runbook. PR: #2345 (WIP). Runbook to include: preflight checklist, abort criteria, smoke tests, post-promote verification queries, roll-forward vs rollback steps.

jordan: Who's owning the copier? I can take initial spike on the copier job if needed.

maya: @jordan please own copier. @sahil pls own trace/metric instrumentation. @becka pls author the SLA gating thresholds with product. I'll coordinate rollout and be oncall during promotion window.

becka: I'll draft the gating thresholds in the product doc and link to #runbooks. Need to confirm our rollback SLAs with support team.

oliver: Two more practical notes: 1) keep the compatibility API shallow — only the fields we need for runtime routing, 2) add a short-circuit flag to route 100% to old service quickly (fast kill).

maya: Agreed. We'll also ship a feature-flagged short-circuit key in config service for immediate switch.

jordan: We should avoid schema drift during dual-write. Suggest adding a lightweight adapter that translates new -> old fields so writes remain stable.

maya: Yes — adapter will live in a thin library used by both services. We'll version it and pin per-release.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: branch/feature/maya/cut-and-mend -> staging at 2023-11-02T10:15Z :rocket: (just a heads up)

sahil: After staging tests, let's run a 10k synthetic traffic run with varied seq lengths and token mixes. I can script that.

maya: Timeline proposal: week 0 — instrumentation + copier job + compatibility API on staging; week 1 — dual-write in staging + canary in staging; week 2 — production canaries and gradual promotion. Two-week window but can be extended.

becka: Product: we should notify top customers and have a support standby. Also update public SDK changelog if any behavioral changes can surface.

jordan: Risk list: KV copy lag, unexpected cache pressure, increased tail latency, consumer backpressure. Mitigations noted.

oliver: One final ask — record a short demo walkthrough after the first staging run so platform and infra teams can replicate the process. Video + short writeup.

maya: Will do. I'll post the PR and the runbook in this thread once created. For now, action items: jordan(copy job), sahil(obs), becka(SLA/gates), oliver(canary gating + demo), maya(rollout coord).

becka: :thumbsup: let's schedule a 30m sync Fri to lock the windows once PR is up.

jordan: :eyes: thanks — I'll start the copier spike today and post progress.

maya: Thanks team. Keeping this thread as source-of-truth for the playbook so we can iterate.
